heroText: Jyväskylä is a lake city in Central Finland, known for Alvar Aalto architecture, university life and Rally Finland roads. Start at the Alvar Aalto Museum, climb Harju Ridge for views, then walk Lutakko harbour and Lake Jyväsjärvi. Jyväskylä Airport is small, so rail connections from Helsinki are often practical.

areas.name: City centre
areas.text: The centre is best for first stays, restaurants, shops, the station and easy walks to Harju Ridge.

areas.name: Lutakko
areas.text: Lutakko is the lakeside harbour district, good for events, waterfront walks and modern apartment stays.

areas.name: Kuokkala
areas.text: Kuokkala sits across the lake with residential calm, bridge views and access to local services.
areas.bestFor: quiet stays, lake views, longer visits

areas.name: Kortepohja
areas.text: Kortepohja is useful for university-related stays, budget apartments and access toward the Aalto campus.

airports.name: Jyväskylä Airport (JYV)
airports.text: Jyväskylä Airport is north of the city near Tikkakoski; flight schedules are limited, so check rail alternatives.

airportTransfer.value: 20-30 min by taxi or arranged transfer from Jyväskylä Airport
airportTransfer.note: rail from Helsinki is often more practical
airportTransfer.distance: about 22 km north of the centre

stayOverview: Stay in the city centre for restaurants and station access, Lutakko for lakefront events, Kuokkala for calmer waterside stays, or Kortepohja for university visits and apartment value.
hotelIntro: Jyväskylä is compact around the lake and ridge. Central hotels are easiest, Lutakko suits events and harbour walks, and university-side districts make more sense for longer or purpose-led stays.
rentalCars: A car helps for Rally Finland roads, Säynätsalo and lake-country trips, but not for the compact centre.

history.text: However, the name Jyväsjoki was registered in 1506 for the region's first known resident, Heikki Ihanninpoika Jyväsjoki.
According to the oldest available taxation documents (maakirja), there were seven estates on the Jyväskylä region in 1539.
A shorter form of the name, Jyväs (written Jyuexe) was mentioned slightly earlier in 1565 and again (this time written Jyues) in 1570.
The oldest estate in Jyväskylä continuously held by the same family is the estate of Lahti, which emerged when the estate of Mattila was split between two brothers in 1600.
The City of Jyväskylä was founded on 22 March 1837, when Emperor of Russia and Grand Duke of Finland, Nicholas I of Russia, signed the charter of the city and the infrastructure was essentially.
The first three Finnish-speaking schools in the world were founded in Jyväskylä, the lycée in 1858, the teachers’ college in 1863, and the girls’ school in 1864.

history.label: 20th century
history.text: In the early 20th century, the town expanded several times.
Säynätsalo was consolidated with Jyväskylä in 1993, and Jyväskylän maalaiskunta and Korpilahti, for their part, on January 1, 2009.

history.label: 21st century
